text: Hello everyone, welcome to my class.Today we are going to learn critical thinking, grouping information.By the end of this lesson, you are expected to 1.Develop the ability to group and present key information with the help of a table.Have a better understanding of how natural descriptions can help convey writer's feelings.Now, please get your textbooks and worksheets ready.Ok, let's get started.This unit revolves around nature, and you have come into contact with all sorts of things in nature.For example, in reading A, the huge tree that is withered and dry has stuck in my mind because of its central importance to the garden.So what things in nature have seized your attention in this unit?Ok, let's start from reading A.What has seized your attention?Peter says he has seen flowers.What kind of flowers?In paragraph 4, it is said that plants and flowers disappeared and withered, so we have withered flowers.Meanwhile, in paragraph 6, we have flourishing flowers.Peter also noticed that in paragraph 6, there appear brightly colored birds and colorful worms.Next, let's move on to listening and viewing.The songwriter of What a Wonderful World sings the praises of the ordinary miracles in everyday life.So what things in nature have you identified in this song?Plenty of them, right?Linda is attracted by green trees, blooming red roses, blue skies, white clouds, bright blessed days and dark sacred nights.What about the video Nature Makes You Happy?What in the scenes has captured your attention?Jane says she is impressed by the great diversity of animals on this planet, and she spots chimpanzees and giraffes.Then what about reading B?This passage is scattered with description of natural beauty.So what things in nature particularly appeal to you?OK, Jack wants to share his opinion.He can still recall the image of a sky aflame at sunset, a rainbow, mountains and seas, moonlight on a starry night, and leaves budding on a tree.Now we have a pool of words for things in nature.If you hope to present all the information in a clear and neat form, you can use a table like this one on page 15 of your textbook.Please put the things in nature into different categories.You will have two minutes for it.搅拌均匀,并搅拌均匀,并搅拌均匀。So, how do the rest of these things in nature usually make us feel?Do we have any volunteer?OK, Owen wants to try.He thinks a withered and dry tree may make him feel gloomy.And the same applies to withered flowers.Oh, Owen adds that these withered trees and flowers also make us feel regretful, since they remind us of our irresponsible attitude toward nature.Great!In fact, when you hope to describe how the things in nature make you feel, you may find these sentences quite helpful.For example, the sight of a withered dry tree makes us feel gloomy, or seeing a withered dry tree one may feel gloomy, or the sight of a withered dry tree evokes the feeling of gloom, or when a withered dry tree comes into view, it fills our heart with gloom.Aren't they useful tools?Now, do we have more volunteers?Alright, Linda thinks, seeing flourishing flowers, green trees and blooming red roses, one may feel cheerful.Sam says, the sight of a sky aflame at sunset evokes the feeling of amazement.He also says, when the moonlight on a starry night comes into view, it fills our heart with romance.Now, you are quite skilled in using these sentence patterns to describe the feelings.But have you noticed that sometimes the same thing in nature might trigger different feelings?For example, as you have heard, flowers can evoke the feeling of both gloom and cheer.What is it that has made the difference?That's right, withered flowers and flourishing flowers evoke distinct feelings because these two phrases feature distinct qualifiers, which are words used to describe the feature of something.So, it is not necessarily the thing itself, but the words used to describe them, such as withered and flourishing, that can inspire a certain feeling in us.For example, do leaves always make us hopeful?Not necessarily.Can you come up with an instance where leaves make us feel gloomy?Right!Fallen leaves may symbolize death and thus evoke the feeling of gloom.Because things in nature can be carriers of various feelings, they have made their way into poetry and lyrics since ancient times.Poets and songwriters find it practical to use these images to convey feelings because these natural things are an intrinsic part of our lives, so we can easily relate to the feelings they convey.Let's take this poem as an example.It is the English version of an Asian Chinese poem.Can you guess which one it is?Good!It is A Spring Morning written by Meng Haoran.Here is the Chinese version.So, in this poem, what things in nature are involved?We can see morning, spring, birds, night, storm, and blossoms.What feelings do these images help convey?OK, James wants to have a try.According to James, from the first two lines, we can see that the poet feels light-hearted when he wakes up surrounded by the singing of birds.So the poet is inspired not just by birds, but singing birds, with their lively and cheerful tunes.By using this image, the vigor and liveliness of spring comes to our mind.So we can sense that the poet takes delight in the beauty of spring.Then, from the last two lines, signaled by the transitional word, but, a different feeling emerges.In contrast to the singing of birds in the morning, the poet recalls the storm at night which broke spring blossoms.Storms are often associated with mighty destructive power that arouses fear and awe.Here, the storm destroyed the blossoms.Blossoms usually convey cheerful and hopeful feelings.So, when they are broken, they imply that the cheer and hope of spring is destined to come to an end, and thus they make us feel sad and gloomy.We can sense the poet's regret of the departure of spring.To group the ideas James has come up with, we can produce a table like this.At the end of the previous class, you were asked to collect poems or songs about nature.Now, it's time that you made an analysis of your poems or songs to figure out what feelings are conveyed.You need to identify the things in nature and pay attention to important qualifiers of the natural things.You have three minutes.
